subject: ela
cluster: Range of reading and level of text complexity

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Bears have thick fur and a layer of fat under their skin. These help bears stay warm during cold winters. In fall, bears eat as much food as they can to build up fat before hibernating.

What is this passage mostly about?
items.answer: The passage is mostly about how bears prepare for and survive cold winters.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

The Nile River is one of the longest rivers in the world. It flows through northeastern Africa and empties into the Mediterranean Sea. Ancient Egyptians built their civilization along its banks.

Name two facts the article tells you about the Nile River.
items.answer: Fact 1: The Nile River is one of the longest rivers in the world. Fact 2: It flows through northeastern Africa and empties into the Mediterranean Sea. (Accept any two facts from the passage.)

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

How to Wash Your Hands:
Step 1: Turn on the water and wet your hands.
Step 2: Put soap on your hands and scrub for at least 20 seconds.
Step 3: Rinse all the soap off your hands.
Step 4: Dry your hands with a clean towel.

What is the purpose of this text?
items.answer: The purpose of this text is to give instructions (how-to steps) for washing your hands correctly.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Salt Lake City is the capital of Utah. It sits in a valley surrounded by mountains. The Great Salt Lake, one of the largest saltwater lakes in the Western Hemisphere, is nearby.

What is the main topic of this passage?
items.answer: The main topic is Salt Lake City and its location in Utah near mountains and the Great Salt Lake.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Marie Curie was a scientist who studied radioactivity. She was born in Poland in 1867. She moved to France to study at university because Polish universities did not accept women at the time. She went on to win two Nobel Prizes.

Where was Marie Curie born?
items.answer: Marie Curie was born in Poland.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Hummingbirds are the smallest birds in the world. Some species weigh less than a penny. They can beat their wings up to 80 times per second and are the only birds that can fly backward.

Name one special ability that hummingbirds have.
items.answer: Hummingbirds can fly backward. (Also accept: they can beat their wings up to 80 times per second.)

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

The water cycle has three main parts. First, the sun heats water in lakes and oceans and it rises into the air as vapor. Then the vapor cools and forms clouds. Finally, the water falls back to the ground as rain or snow.

What happens first in the water cycle?
items.answer: First, the sun heats water in lakes and oceans and it rises into the air as vapor.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Seahorse fathers carry their babies. After a female seahorse lays her eggs in a pouch on the male's belly, the male keeps the eggs safe until they hatch. A male seahorse can give birth to up to 1,000 babies at one time.

What is unusual about how seahorses have babies?
items.answer: It is unusual that the father, not the mother, carries the eggs and gives birth to the babies.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

The sun rises in the east and sets in the west every day. This happens because Earth spins on its axis once every 24 hours. As Earth spins, different parts of it face the sun, which is why we have day and night.

Why do we have day and night?
items.answer: We have day and night because Earth spins on its axis. As it spins, different parts of Earth face the sun, causing day on the side facing the sun and night on the other side.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Earthworms help make soil healthy. As they move through the ground, they break up hard soil and create tunnels that let in air and water. Their waste, called castings, adds nutrients that plants need to grow.

How do earthworms help plants?
items.answer: Earthworms help plants by breaking up hard soil, creating tunnels for air and water, and adding nutrients to the soil through their waste (castings).

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

How to Make a Fruit Salad:
Step 1: Wash the fruit.
Step 2: Cut the fruit into small pieces with help from an adult.
Step 3: Put all the fruit pieces into a bowl.
Step 4: Stir gently and serve.

What should you do before cutting the fruit?
items.answer: You should wash the fruit before cutting it (Step 1 comes before Step 2).

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

The Amazon rainforest is called the 'lungs of the Earth.' It produces a large amount of the world's oxygen. The Amazon also receives more rainfall than almost any other place on Earth.

Why is the Amazon called the 'lungs of the Earth'?
items.answer: The Amazon is called the 'lungs of the Earth' because it produces a large amount of the world's oxygen, just as lungs produce oxygen for a living body.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

John Muir was born in Scotland in 1838. As a young man, he moved to California and fell in love with the wild mountains and forests. He spent years exploring and writing about nature. His writing helped convince the government to protect Yosemite as a national park.

What was one important thing John Muir helped accomplish?
items.answer: John Muir helped convince the government to protect Yosemite as a national park.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Ice floats on water because it is less dense than liquid water. Most substances become denser when they freeze, but water is unusual. When water freezes into ice, the molecules arrange themselves in a way that takes up more space, making it lighter per unit of volume.

What is unusual about water compared to most other substances?
items.answer: Unlike most substances, water becomes less dense when it freezes, which is why ice floats on liquid water.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Mosquitoes are more than just annoying insects. They can spread serious diseases like malaria, dengue fever, and Zika virus when they bite. Mosquitoes are considered one of the most dangerous animals in the world because of the illnesses they carry.

Why are mosquitoes considered dangerous?
items.answer: Mosquitoes are considered dangerous because they can spread serious diseases like malaria, dengue fever, and Zika virus when they bite people.
